# Bat roost exercise
![](/images/bat_1.png){style="width:200px"}
First we will look at the file [bat_roosts.csv](https://neof-workshops.github.io/R_j4c0xh/downloads/bat_roosts.csv). This contains information on the max number of roosts for different Bat species in different UK regions. The data is from: "Bat Conservation Trust 2020. Roost Count peak counts summary data". Available from https://www.bats.org.uk/our-work/national-bat-monitoring-programme/reports/nbmp-annual-report Solutions are in the expandable boxes. Try your best to solve each challenge but use the solutions for help if you would like. Even if your method works it can be good to check the solution as there are many ways to do the same thing in R ## Bat roost challenges ### Bat roost challenge 1 {-}
![](/images/bat_2.png){style="width:100px"}
__Read__ in the file "bat_roosts.csv" as a __data frame__ __variable__ called "bat_df". Ensure the row names contain the Regions (Channel Islands, East Midlands, etc.).
Read in the file as a __data frame__: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bat_df <- read.csv("Chapter_8_files/bat_roosts.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE) ``` :::
### Bat roost challenge 2 {-}
![](/images/bat_3.png){style="width:100px"}
Inspect the __variable__ and ensure there are only numerics within the __data frame__ with all strings only being in column and row names. ### Bat roost challenge 3 {-}
![](/images/bat_4.png){style="width:100px"}
Add a row to "bat_df" called "UK" that contains the totals for each Species.
Add a row with column totals: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bat_df["UK",] <- colSums(bat_df) ``` :::
### Bat roost challenge 4 {-}
![](/images/bat_5.png){style="width:100px"}
Add a column to "bat_df" called "All_Bat_Species" that contains the totals for each Region.
Create transposed __data frame__: Add a column with row totals: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bat_df$All_Bat_Species <- rowSums(bat_df) ``` :::
### Bat roost challenge 5 {-}
![](/images/bat_6.png){style="width:100px"}
Create a transposed __data frame__ of "bat_df" called "bat_t_df".
Create transposed __data frame__: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bat_t_df <- as.data.frame(t(bat_df)) ``` :::
### Bat roost challenge 6 {-}
![](/images/bat_7.png){style="width:100px"}
__Write__ the __data frame__ "bat_t_df" to a comma separated file called "bat_roosts_t.csv". Ensure there are no quotes surrounding the row or column names.
__Write__ file: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write.table(bat_t_df, file = "Chapter_8_files/bat_roosts_t.csv", sep = ",", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA) ``` :::
## Bat roost MCQs
![](/images/question_bubble_purple.png){style="width:150px; background: white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px"}
Fantastic! I hope those challenges were engaging and improved your experience working with files and data frames. Attempt the following MCQs using your final "bat_t_df" object. ::: {.cell} ::: 1. Which region has no roosts?
::: {.cell} ::: 2. Which region has the largest amount of _Myotis brandtii_ roosts (excluding UK)?
::: {.cell} ::: 3. Which Bat species has the highest number of roosts across the UK?
::: {.cell} ::: 4. Which Bat species has the lowest number of roosts across the UK?
You can figure out the MCQs by viewing the data frame. However, you can also figure them out with R code. Below are commands to get the answers for the MCQs. I will let you decipher them yourself. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 1: Which region has no roosts? col_names_logical_vec <- bat_t_df["All_Bat_Species",] == 0 colnames(bat_t_df)[col_names_logical_vec] ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 2: Which region has the largest amount of Myotis brandtii roosts? species <- "Myotis brandtii" df_wo_total_species_and_uk <- bat_t_df[ 1:(nrow(bat_t_df)-1),1:(ncol(bat_t_df)-1)] max_colonies <- max(df_wo_total_species_and_uk[species,]) col_names_logical_vec <- df_wo_total_species_and_uk[species,] == max_colonies colnames(df_wo_total_species_and_uk)[col_names_logical_vec] ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 3: Which Bat species has the highest number of roosts across the UK? max_uk <- max(bat_t_df[1:(nrow(bat_t_df)-1),"UK"]) row_names_logical_vec <- bat_t_df$UK == max_uk row.names(bat_t_df)[row_names_logical_vec] ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Question 4: Which Bat species has the lowest number of roosts across the UK? min_uk <- min(bat_t_df[1:(nrow(bat_t_df)-1),"UK"]) row_names_logical_vec <- bat_t_df$UK == min_uk row.names(bat_t_df)[row_names_logical_vec] ``` :::
